title: Flying With the Hurricane Hunters: Part 1
gist: Airman Pulse episode notes: two veterans of the Air Force's 53rd Weather Reconnaissance Squadron, the Hurricane Hunters, trace how they entered one of the Air Force's most unusual jobs and explain why crews still fly manned aircraft into hurricanes even as satellites and forecast models improve.

insights.claim: Air Force Hurricane Hunter crews still fly into hurricanes despite continuing improvement in satellites and forecast models, according to two squadron veterans.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: In-situ measurement retains value over remote sensing and modeling, relevant to weather-data and forecasting capability assumptions.
insights.quote: explain why crews still fly into hurricanes when satellites and forecast models keep getting better

insights.claim: Jon Talbot spent 27 years as an aerial reconnaissance weather officer in the Air Force's 53rd Weather Reconnaissance Squadron.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: Illustrates the depth of niche human expertise underpinning hurricane reconnaissance capability.

insights.claim: Jeff Ragusa flew the WC-130J aircraft and served as the Hurricane Hunters squadron's chief pilot.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: Identifies the WC-130J as the operating platform for U.S. hurricane reconnaissance.
